subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should cron failure reporting for started-but-not-completed runs remain restart-aware and Gateway-local, or should OpenClaw add an external or supervisor-backed alert path for wedged Gateway processes?
rationale: Current code can mark interrupted jobs failed after restart, but the issue asks for user-visible notification when memory pressure or event-loop delay prevents normal Gateway-local delivery; that is an architecture and product reliability boundary.

options.title: Validate current main first
options.body: Run the macOS launchd soak on the reported memory and cron workload, then choose a narrower fix only if the silent gap still reproduces.

options.title: Design supervisor-backed alerts
options.body: Add an out-of-process or host-supervised cron lifecycle monitor so failure reporting can survive a wedged Gateway event loop.

options.title: Split trackers now
options.body: Keep this as a parent and open separate canonical items for memory growth, restart recovery, and cron alert semantics.

recommendation.title: Validate current main first
recommendation.body: Run the macOS launchd soak on the reported memory and cron workload, then choose a narrower fix only if the silent gap still reproduces.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the merged memory-core FD fix and adjacent review history, and the remaining choice spans memory reliability and product recovery behavior.
